{{nihongo|'''Kawase Shrine'''|河瀬神社 (彦根市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Kawase Shrine''' (かわせじんじゃ) is a shrine in {{ill|Hikone, Shiga|Q386635|qid=Q386635}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is treated as a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for "Kawaketa Shrine" of Kanzaki District, {{ill|Ōmi Province|ca|Província d'Ōmi|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆمی|cs|Provincie Ómi|de|Provinz Ōmi|es|Provincia de Ōmi|fa|ولایت اومی|fi|Ōmin provinssi|fr|Province d'Ōmi|gl|Provincia de Ōmi|hak|Ōmi-koet|id|Provinsi Ōmi|it|Ōmi|ja|近江国|ko|오미국|lt|Omio žemė|nl|Omi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Ōmi|pt|Província de Ōmi|ru|Оми (провинция)|simple|Ōmi Province|sk|Ómi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Оми|tr|Ōmi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Омі|vi|Tỉnh Ōmi|zh|近江國|zh_min_nan|Ômi-kok|zh_yue|近江國|qid=Q843882}}, listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' (a candidate {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}})<ref>As candidate shrines for "Kawaketa Shrine," six are known: {{ill|Kawaketamikabe Shrine|Q11553975|qid=Q11553975}} (Kanda-chō, Yōkaichi, now {{ill|Higashiōmi|Q240891|qid=Q240891}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Obata Shrine}} (Gokashō Nakamachi, Higashiōmi), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtaki Shrine}} (Kayao-chō, Higashiōmi), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawawaki Shrine}} (Nakajuku, {{ill|Aishō, Shiga|Q1346806|qid=Q1346806}}, Aichi District), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawaketa Shrine}} (Kōsaki-chō, Hikone), and this shrine in the former Inukami District.</ref>. It was formerly ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316|lt=gōsha}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} are three {{ill|Column|Q4817|qid=Q4817}}: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|qid=Q10935105|lt=Ōyamakui-no-Mikoto}}. If this shrine was the Engishiki "Kawaketa Shrine," many theories hold that the original deity was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Yukawaketa-no-Mikoto}}<ref>For example: {{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|Q108780926|qid=Q108780926}}, '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|Q11588824|qid=Q11588824}}'; {{ill|Kurita Hiroshi|Q6536170|qid=Q6536170}}, '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jingishi-ryō}}'; '{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}'; and '{{ill|Dai Nihonshi|Q1156003|qid=Q1156003|lt=Dai Nihon Shi Jingi-shi}}'. '{{ill|Ōmi Yochi Shiryaku|Q85883966|qid=Q85883966}}' identifies this shrine as the Shikinaisha but does not state the enshrined deity, and '{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}' says "deity unknown."</ref>.

It has long been worshiped as a deity of commerce. Because "Kawase" can also be read as "exchange," it also attracts worship from people in finance.

=== History ===
The founding date is unknown, but until the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called "Kawaketa Shrine," "Keta-no-miya," and "Keta Daimyōjin."<ref name="#1">{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.hikone.shiga.jp/kikakushinkobu/johoseisaku/pdf/20120501KH08.pdf Kōhō Hikone, May 1 2012 issue, p.17, serial feature: My town in the Sengoku era, No.22 - Kawase Castle - flatland fort linked to the Kawase clan]}}</ref> In {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} 1 ({{ill|1570|Q6659|qid=Q6659}}), the lords of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawase-no-shō}}<ref>[http://kids.city.hikone.shiga.jp/carta/card_so.html Hikone City Hall: Learn Hikone history through karuta]</ref>, the Kawase clan, repaired the shrine buildings and donated rice fields. Through the Edo period it was revered by the Ii lords of {{ill|Hikone Domain|Q1062225|qid=Q1062225}}, and at major festivals a {{ill|Bugyō|Q2535820|qid=Q2535820}} was dispatched for ceremonial security<ref>'Shintō Daijiten.'</ref>. According to "Jinja Yūshoki" compiled by Shiga Prefecture's education section, in {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} 3 ({{ill|1675|Q7624|qid=Q7624}}), Kawase Iki-no-kami and his grandson Kawase Hayato-no-shō, former local lords of Kawase-no-shō, re-established the shrine by inviting {{ill|Aidono|Q135009883|qid=Q135009883|lt=aiden deities}}<ref>Which deity/deities these aiden referred to is unknown.</ref>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} era it was renamed "Kawase Shrine." It was ranked gōsha on January 17, Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), temporarily demoted to {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} on October 21, Meiji 9, restored to gōsha again on February 1, Meiji 14, and designated as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and cloth}} on April 29, Meiji 41. A 2012 survey by Hikone City's cultural-properties section estimated nearby remains to be those of {{ill|Kawase Castle|Q11554012|qid=Q11554012}}.<ref name="#1"/>

=== Precinct shrines ===
Isorowa Shrine, Hachiman Shrine, Wakamatsu Shrine, Hachidai Shrine, Tennei Shrine, Kaminoki Shrine, Tsujinaka Shrine, Tenmangū-sha, Tenman Shrine

=== Precinct ===
* Monument to Tanemura Genpei (Horsehead commemorative stele)

=== Access ===
* From {{ill|Kawase Station|arz|محطة كاواس|eo|Stacio Kawase|fr|Gare de Kawase|it|Stazione di Kawase|ja|河瀬駅|ko|가와세역|my|ခဝဆဲဘူတာ|nl|Station Kawase|ur|کاوارسے اسٹیشن|zh|河瀨車站|qid=Q614782}} on the {{ill|Biwako Line|de|Biwako-Linie|eo|Linio Biwako|es|Línea Biwako|fr|Ligne Biwako|hu|Bivako-vonal|it|Linea Biwako|ja|琵琶湖線|ko|비와코선|nl|JR Biwako-lijn|th|สายบิวาโกะ|vi|Tuyến Biwako|zh|琵琶湖線|qid=Q804135}} ({{ill|Tōkaidō Main Line|de|Tōkaidō-Hauptlinie|eo|Linio Tōkaidō (ĉefa)|fa|خط اصلی توکایدو|fr|Ligne principale Tōkaidō|hu|Tókaidó-vasútvonal|id|Jalur Utama Tōkaidō|it|Linea principale Tōkaidō|ja|東海道本線|ko|도카이도 본선|nl|Tokaido-lijn|no|Tōkaidōlinjen|pt|Linha principal Tōkaidō|ru|Линия Токайдо|su|Jalur Utama Tōkaidō|sv|Tokaidolinjen|th|สายหลักโทไกโด|tl|Pangunahing Linyang Tōkaidō|tr|Tōkaidō Ana Hattı|vi|Tuyến Tōkaidō chính|wuu|东海道本线|zh|東海道本線|zh_yue|東海道本線|qid=Q1190152}}), take the reservation-only Ainori Taxi Kawase to Kawasebabachō Kōminkan stop; 2 minutes on foot.
* About 12 minutes on foot from Kawase Station.
